title: Model Catalog demo - Meridian Health
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Meridian Health through the Model Catalog in the Console: filtering/selecting open models, interpreting benchmark tiles (latency/cost/quality), and mapping compatibility to their on-prem GPU fleet. Customer cares about clinical context length (8k-32k), SOC2/KMS, and predictable latency for triage workflows. Agreed next steps: share compatibility matrix, benchmark spreadsheet, pricing for Dedicated, and schedule POC scoping.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia from Redwood, with Daniel our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:00:12] Priya Patel: Priya here, CTO at Meridian. We run clinical triage workflows, primary goal is low latency on 8k contexts and data residency.
[00:00:20] Ethan Ross: Ethan, head of ML; we're evaluating open models first, cost is big.
[00:00:28] Daniel Cho: Great, I'll share my screen and jump into the Model Catalog in the Console. Warning: my wifi is meh, so may stutter.
[00:00:40] Daniel Cho: (screen) So here is the Model Catalog — you can filter by family, license, verified performance. We tag models with benchmark tiles: median p50 latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and a quality score for summarization/QA.
[00:01:05] Lena Ortiz: Can you filter to permissive-licensed open models only?
[00:01:10] Daniel Cho: Yep, filter -> license -> permissive. Now you see a short list: redwood/curie-open (example), mpt-8k, falcon-40b-instruct (quant variants). Note: some model names are approximate in the transcript, the Console shows full repo names.
[00:01:28] Sofia Martinez: Important to call out our 'verified' tag — we've run standardized benchmarks on our infra and report latency/cost curves across sequence lengths (512/2k/8k/32k).
[00:01:45] Ethan Ross: How do you measure quality? We care about clinical accuracy on triage prompts.
[00:01:50] Daniel Cho: We run eval sets — you can upload your prompt set and run QuickEval to get macro F1/answer accuracy and also generate confusion examples. For default tiles we use public evals but recommend private evals for clinical.
[00:02:10] Aisha Khan: Security question — if we go Dedicated or Private, can we integrate our KMS and SAML?
[00:02:16] Sofia Martinez: Yes — Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and SAML/SSO. Private on-prem supports HSM and full VPC isolated control plane. We'll share SOC2 docs and an architecture note.
[00:02:30] Noah Kim: For compatibility: we run A100/RTX6000 equivalent on-prem; do you have a matrix for quantization/throughput tradeoffs?
[00:02:38] Daniel Cho: Absolutely, in the catalog each model has a compatibility matrix: which accelerators it's been tested on, supported precisions (fp16/int8/int4 experimental), and expected KV cache memory for X tokens. Eg, falcon-40b int8 reduces GPU memory ~50% but watch quality delta, we flag models with regression risks.
[00:03:03] Ethan Ross: Can Redwood fallback to a smaller model if Dedicated capacity is saturated?
[00:03:07] Sofia Martinez: Yes, smart routing can fall back to a compatible variant (e.g., 40b -> 7b) with canary rollouts and automatic A/B. Fallback policies are configurable per route.
[00:03:20] Daniel Cho: Back to the Console — clicking a model opens a detail page: benchmark strip across sequence lengths, 95th percentile tail latency, cost per 1k tokens, and a 'compatibility' tab with supported runtime (A100/T4), quant profiles, kernel notes.
[00:03:40] Daniel Cho: Note the benchmark CSV link on the right; you can download full CSV for your own cost modeling or run it against your prompt set in QuickEval.
[00:03:52] Priya Patel: If we use a long clinical history, say 16k tokens, performance matters more than cost. Will you provide guidance on batching and KV cache strategies?
[00:04:00] Daniel Cho: Yes — Redwood Optimize suggests batching windows and cache prefixes. For high-variance input lengths we recommend prefix caching for common templates and adaptive batching to preserve p50 latency. KV cache memory scales linearly with seq length — we show that in the compatibility view (may appear as "KV cash" typo in quick notes).
[00:04:23] Lena Ortiz: Are there tradeoffs for quantization for clinical safety?
[00:04:26] Daniel Cho: We surface quantization risk flags — models that show quality regressions post-quant are marked. You can request a regression report for your eval set. For clinical, many customers keep fp16 for safety, but int8 is common when cost is constraining.
[00:04:44] Aisha Khan: Does logging include redacted audit logs and enterprise retention controls?
[00:04:48] Sofia Martinez: Yes, Dedicated/Private have configurable audit retention, redaction rules, and immutable logs sent to your SIEM. We'll attach the security pack.
[00:04:58] Ethan Ross: Can you run a quick benchmark for a proxy prompt? Like summarization across a 4k note?
[00:05:02] Daniel Cho: I can run a quick eval but for reliable numbers we usually run a POC job — takes 24-48 hours. We can run a quick sample in-console to show relative latency.
[00:05:15] Daniel Cho: (narrates) Triggering quick eval... result: falcon-40b-instruct (fp16) median 120ms p50 on our hosted rig at 4k, int8 version 95ms but quality dip ~2.1% on the default medical QA set. These are illustrative.
[00:05:40] Priya Patel: That's promising. What about multi-region / data residency?
[00:05:44] Sofia Martinez: We have region controls and can pin traffic to specific cloud regions. Private deployments can be air-gapped.
[00:05:52] Noah Kim: On Dedicated, what's SLA for latency and throughput?
[00:05:56] Sofia Martinez: Dedicated comes with throughput commits and latency SLOs for specific instance types; we include autoscaling burst capacity. I'll share the SLA doc.
[00:06:06] Lena Ortiz: Who do we contact for pricing and committed capacity?
[00:06:10] Sofia Martinez: I'll send Dedicated pricing sheets and commit levels. We also have a pilot offer to validate latency on your infra.
[00:06:18] Ethan Ross: One last: how do you version models? We need reproducibility for audits.
[00:06:23] Daniel Cho: Each catalog entry has model versions, and you can pin exact variants. We also store model provenance and kernel selection notes. Rollouts are versioned and you can rollback.
[00:06:34] Priya Patel: Sounds good. Any known competitors we should worry about for feature parity?
[00:06:38] Sofia Martinez: We often see OpenAI for hosted simplicity, Anthropic for safety-focused models, and self-host stacks like Replicate. I'll include a short competitor comparison.
[00:06:51] Daniel Cho: Quick demo of exporting compatibility matrix as CSV — here you get GPU tested, precision, memory footprint per token, and recommended quant profile; you can import this into your capacity planner.
[00:07:10] Aisha Khan: We'll need SOC2 report and KMS integration doc.
[00:07:14] Sofia Martinez: Noted — we'll attach those.
[00:07:18] Lena Ortiz: Timeline? We want a POC in Dec if possible.
[00:07:22] Sofia Martinez: We can scope a focused POC to run benchmarks against your prompt set; how about week of Dec 8th for a scoping call?
[00:07:30] Priya Patel: Works for us.
[00:07:33] Sofia Martinez: Recap — Daniel will share compatibility matrix and benchmark CSV; I'll send pricing and security pack; Ethan to provide sample prompts and acceptance criteria; schedule scoping for 12/08.
[00:07:45] Ethan Ross: I'll drop a drive folder with sample prompts by EOD Friday.
[00:07:50] Sofia Martinez: Great. Thanks everyone.
[00:07:54] Priya Patel: Thanks, bye.
[00:07:56] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional ASR errors (SMAL for SAML, KV cash), speaker tags genericized in spots. Full benchmark CSV and compatibility matrix referenced in next steps.
